outcome: Cervical elastography (anterior and posterior strain rate)
cohort: The study included 339 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies, comprising 24 women with a history of cervical insufficiency who underwent cerclage and a control group without cervical insufficiency.
finding: Even after cerclage, women with cervical insufficiency had softer anterior and posterior cervical lips and shorter cervical length compared to controls, and softer anterior cervical lip and shorter cervical length were significantly related to preterm delivery.
followup_time: Until preterm delivery (for the outcome of preterm delivery), measurements were taken in the second trimester.
